full_caption: Kingsmere Property Group, Inc., Appellant, v. Perrin Umberton, Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: The parties own adjoining parcels on Kingfisher Drive. The dispute concerns a strip approximately 30 feet in width lying between the fence line maintained since 1986 and the line described in the parties' respective deeds.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: A quiet-title plaintiff must recover on the strength of its own title and not on the weakness of the defendant's. Kingsmere Property Group, Inc. traced an unbroken chain to the 2002 patent and thereby carried that burden as to the residue of the parcel.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: The surveyor called by Kingsmere Property Group, Inc. located the original iron pin at the southeast corner and retraced the line from that monument. The surveyor called by Perrin Umberton began from a subdivision plat computation without locating any original monument.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: The doctrine of acquiescence establishes a boundary where adjoining owners have recognized and treated a visible line as the boundary for the statutory period, regardless of what the deeds provide.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: Perrin Umberton had constructive notice of the disputed occupation. Possession that is open and visible puts a purchaser on inquiry as to the rights of the possessor, and a purchaser who fails to inquire is charged with what inquiry would have disclosed.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: A retracement that ignores an original monument capable of being located is entitled to little weight. We accept the trial court's finding crediting the monument-based survey.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: The recording act of this State is a race-notice statute. A subsequent purchaser for value prevails over a prior unrecorded interest only if the purchaser took without notice and recorded first.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: The trial court's reformation of the deed to correct a scrivener's transposition of the bearing from N 57°40' E to N 86°43' E is supported by clear and convincing evidence of mutual mistake.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: The fence erected in 1986 was maintained jointly, and both households mowed to their respective sides without objection until Kingsmere Property Group, Inc. obtained the 1991 survey. That course of conduct satisfies the acquiescence standard.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: Where a deed description conflicts with monuments actually set on the ground, the monuments control. Calls in a conveyance are given priority in the order: natural monuments, artificial monuments, courses, distances, and quantity.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: Acquiescence requires (1) occupation up to a visible line, (2) mutual recognition of that line as the boundary, and (3) continuance for 10 years. Silence coupled with occupation may supply the element of mutual recognition.

sections.heading: Paragraph 12
sections.text: The judgment quieting title in Kingsmere Property Group, Inc. to the disputed strip is affirmed. The counterclaim for trespass damages is remanded for a determination of the value of the removed timber.

sections.heading: RIDER II — SURVEY AND MONUMENTATION
sections.text: The agreed line shall be monumented with iron pins set at each angle point and at intervals not exceeding 30 feet, and a plat of the survey shall be filed with the Rooksbury County Recorder. In the event of conflict between this description and the monuments as set, the monuments shall control.

sections.heading: RIDER IV — ENCROACHMENT LICENSE
sections.text: The parties acknowledge that the carport encroaches approximately 1.5 feet onto the adjoining parcel. The adjoining owner grants a revocable license permitting the encroachment to remain until the structure is removed, destroyed, or substantially rebuilt, at which time the license terminates automatically and the structure shall be reconstructed wholly within the boundary.

sections.heading: RIDER V — MUTUAL RELEASE AND QUIET ENJOYMENT
sections.text: Each party releases the other from all claims for trespass, ejectment, or damage to the disputed strip arising before the date of this agreement, and covenants not to disturb the other's quiet enjoyment of the land lying on that party's side of the agreed line.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Insurance
sections.text: The party in possession shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence, naming the other party as an additional insured, and shall furnish a certificate of insurance on request and on each renewal. Each party waives subrogation against the other to the extent of insurance proceeds actually received.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Indemnity
sections.text: Each party shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the other from all claims, damages and expenses, including reasonable attorney's fees, arising out of that party's use of the subject premises or breach of this instrument, except to the extent caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of the party seeking indemnity. This clause survives termination.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Entire Agreement and Riders
sections.text: This instrument, together with the exhibits and riders attached and incorporated by reference, constitutes the entire agreement of the parties and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations and agreements, whether oral or written. In the event of a conflict between a printed provision and a rider, the rider shall control, the rider being the specifically negotiated expression of the parties' intent.
